name: PTC Extreme Championship
epitaph: The alliance's hardcore championship, first won on 21 July 2002 by Menace of the XCWF, who beat Jackson Rust in the final of the R.E.B.E.L. tournament the XCWF ran with PTC's backing and lost it in August to Rust; Rust was stripped of it when he spoke of retiring. The record then reaches the New Era card of 20 April 2003, where the belt already had a history — the results page calls that night only the second defence in the title's own life. Terry Woods came out of semi-retirement to defend it inside the Death Trap, a suspended ring strung with barbed wire over a burning pit, and lost it to Maelgrim in Maelgrim's own debut match. The title was later vacated when Maelgrim and his challenger Kai Shinobi both failed to show for a title match. Tristan Belmont was champion by 27 September 2003 and lost it to Fathom in a hide and seek match on 5 December; Mike Marvelous took it from Fathom in the Lion's Den at WWA's Fiesta on 19 January 2004, Sean McClancy from Marvelous in the Irish Pub Brawl on 21 April, and Moraless from McClancy on UWF's Sunday Afternoon Supremacy on 23 May, before giving it up in July. Joey Vendetti won the vacant title in the Elimination Chamber at PTC Survival on 22 August 2004, Shadow took it from him in a three-way on 22 February 2005, and Nova took it from Shadow in a scaffold match at PRIME's Overkill on 15 May; Nova vacated it on 31 August. Hoyt Williams won the vacant title, while Rich “The Renegade” Rollins took the vacant PTC Global Championship, in a Scavenger Hunt Match at PTC's Super Series I on 6 November 2005. Archibald MacGregor, a free agent, took it from him in a judged title match (the forum's own results are dated 4 June 2006; the fed's later write-up says March) and held it until 29 December 2006, when he dropped out of his next defence and the title went to Nova, the first man to hold it twice. Dusk won the last Extreme Title match, an eight-way, on 15 February 2007, and lost the belt to Jason Snow on 30 April 2007, when it was folded into the PTC Unified Championship. PTC's own title log dates three of these wins differently from the hosts' own cards and PTC's own records of the matches — Marvelous's to 21 January 2004, McClancy's to 20 April and Vendetti's to 9 November 2004, the day the results were posted — and puts MacGregor's win on an AWC card of 30 May 2006; the dates above are the cards' and records' own. Who held it before Woods, and how Woods won it, the record does not settle.
notes: The belt's first two reigns are recorded: Menace won it on 21 July 2002 in the final of the R.E.B.E.L. tournament, and lost it about two weeks later to Jackson Rust, who was stripped of it when he spoke of retiring. Which held record Jackson Rust is has not been settled, so his reign carries the name as PTC's own title log bills him. Nothing survives about who held the title, or how, between his reign and Terry Woods's, which begins at a date nobody has located. At New Era, the results page has Rust at ringside helping Maelgrim, taking revenge for "his title loss, which he didn't actually lose".

name: PTC Global Championship
epitaph: The alliance's top prize, defended in an open 128-competitor tournament (eighty signed in the first seventy-two hours) and, by the record's own count, held by sixteen different superstars whose reigns the record places before it was unified with the PTC Extreme Championship on 30 April 2007. Its lineage runs from Vampir Nosferatu's tournament win over Jay Phoenix at PCW's Friday Fusion, through Obsidian, Donny Diamond, three reigns for Seymour Almasy, Chris Storm, Jesse Jamester (who won it from Storm in a four-way crossover title match XUW's own Reborn 2004 show hosted, representing Global Wrestling against Apocalypse and Patti Anderson of Furiously Addictive Wrestling and Four Winds Wrestling), Hessian, Saij, the Latch Key Kid, Emilio Rage, Karina Wolfenden (who vacated it the night she won it), Rich “The Renegade” Rollins, Uber Judge, Shadow and Kimbusa, to Clinton Sage, whose reign ended when Jason Snow won the match that unified the belt with the PTC Extreme Championship. That unified belt, the PTC Unified Championship, now has a record of its own. The sources do not agree on everything: PTC's own title log and PTCpedia date Vampir Nosferatu's win to the final shown on 23 November 2001, where the alliance's news places his reign in February 2002, and the log dates Almasy's win of the title at PTC Survival to 9 November 2004, the day the results were posted, where the show's own billed date is 22 August. The news also has Ignatius Lisieux, who “defeated the dreaded Global Title Curse”, as champion by April 2004, and speaks of a second, unnamed Global Title Tourney winner; PTC's own title log lists neither, so those two reigns stand as the news gives them. Jay Phoenix reached this title's own tournament final once more and lost the judged decision by three points — the closest he came to the biggest prize the whole alliance offered.

name: PTC Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The alliance's tag team championship, first won at the end of a tournament that ran across its member feds for the better part of a year and finished at New Era on 20 April 2003 — Shane Stone and the Bum Boozler, billed as Homo/Phobic, over the Shadow Riders of Lights Out Wrestling. They held it until 3 February 2004, when the Bum Boozler withdrew from tag team competition and the titles were declared vacant. Souls of the Black Lotus won the vacant titles in a three-way on 19 May 2004 and vacated them on 9 July, when the team retired; the Shadow Riders won them at PTC Survival on 22 August 2004 and lost them around 21 December to Clique Clique BOOM~! in a steel cage match decided on the roleplays. The Masked Monkeys of UWF won them on 24 March 2005 and lost them on 26 April to Unholy Matrimony, Seymour Almasy and Aerith Almasy of UWF, in a three-way decided on the judges' scores for the roleplays, which no federation would host and which was never written; the Killer Pirates of the Outer Caribbean took them from Unholy Matrimony uncontested on 28 May, when the champions did not roleplay, and held them until 4 September, when they were vacated because the team was no longer active in PRIME. The record's last word on the belt is the opening match of PTC vs Archibald MacGregor on 15 September 2006, where Unite, billed as the current GCW Tag Team Champions, won the vacant title over the Killer Pirates of the Outer Caribbean; they were the last champions, and the title was retired on 6 January 2007. PTC's own title log dates the Shadow Riders' win to 9 November 2004, the day the results were posted, where the show's own billed date is 22 August.
notes: The fed's own pages style the belt three ways on one night — "PTC Tag Team Titles Match" on the card, "PTC World Tag Team Title Match" as the results' own match header, and "PTC Tag Team Champions" in the commentary that crowned them. Recorded under the shortest form, with the others as aka.

name: PTC Infinite Gauntlet Championship
epitaph: The prize of PTC's Infinite Gauntlet, the forum's perpetual roleplay competition, in which each round's winner stayed on as champion. The Uber Judge took it in the first round on 4 June 2005; twenty-six more reigns followed, twenty-five champions in all, until the last round on 20 December 2010, when the host's replies named James von Doom the last champion. Alcaeus was stripped of it in May 2006, and two champions vacated it.
notes: The fed's own table of champions counts 26 reigns by 24 champions and ends with Eegor; the twenty-seventh reign here is read from the host's replies of 20 December 2010 and is graded presumed.

name: PTC Unified Championship
epitaph: The belt PTC made on 30 April 2007 by unifying its Global and Extreme Titles, in a match decided by judges on the roleplays. Jason Snow won it that day; Clinton Sage, Tchu and Lindsay Troy held it after him, each winning it on another federation's card. Lindsay Troy was the last champion: the title was retired in May 2008.
notes: PTC's own title log dates the retirement to a forum post of 13 May 2008; PTCpedia gives 14 May.

name: PTC Universal Championship
epitaph: Made for Angelo Deville after he won GTT3, PTC's third Golden Turnbuckle Tournament, in 2002. PCW's Alliances card of 24 November 2002 bills it as the WT Universal Championship; Deville kept it there against Xavier Kannon, then against Syko Arsonist on a DWO special event, and lost it to Alan Kriegman on OSW's Saturday Night Slam, four judges' votes to three. A round robin to find Kriegman a challenger was called off unfinished. PTC's history of its Global Championship leaves this belt out.
notes: Angelo Deville's PRIME biography card; PCW's Alliances 2002 card; PTCpedia's GTT history; PTC forum posts 132383, 141903, 170608 and 120404 (Deville's own account), 297925 (Syko Arsonist: "the only PTC vs WT match for the Universal Title") and 241787 (the PTCpedia editor: the Universal and Global titles "were separate belts").

name: PTC Tag Team Tournament
epitaph: A tag-team tournament the alliance ran on an earlier board of its own, whose brackets and final do not survive; what survives of it is the team it crowned, attested by a contributor who wrestled it and by a beaten opponent answering him in the alliance's own forum two years later. The alliance's own board carries a further tag-team tournament, whose final was judged in April 2004, so this was not the only one it ran.

name: PTC Cruiserweight Tournament
epitaph: Open to cruiserweights only, run twice: CW1 in 2004 (forty-two entrants across four brackets, free agents permitted alongside PTC and member-fed competitors) and CW2 in 2005, the smallest tournament in the alliance's history at thirty-two entrants. Seymour Almasy's CW1 win extended a run that reached fourteen straight tournament victories across the PIT, CW1 and GTT4 before ending in GTT4's fourth round.
